flags.t: JD filter O-ring went missing on Tuesday
flags.d: Mitch, 10 Nov in #spraying: the JD filter O-ring was misplaced in Tuesday's clean-up, and that tank ran with the filter out because GreenLinks clogged it. A new O-ring has to be in before this tank goes in. It's the first rig check.

flags.t: Decontaminate the JD before anything else goes in it
flags.d: Firepower (haloxyfop) kills couch and bent at very low doses. The JD is the greens and fairway sprayer: tank cleaner and a triple rinse through tank, boom and filters before it goes on anything else. It's on the post-application checklist.

Firepower kills couch, so any overlap or drift onto fairway edges will show. Wind ESE 7–11 km/h through the morning pushes drift to the west side of each rough: keep section control on the boundaries and the boom low.

flags.t: Buff-It: no label or SDS on file
flags.d: Handled as an acidifier (goggles, elbow gloves) with a 'drum label read' tick. It goes in first; haloxyfop's ester is more stable in buffered water.

Firepower 900 is registered for forestry and industrial grass control, not turf; 90 g/ha haloxyfop here is under its label rates, which Victoria allows off-label. Its label doesn't list fescue as tolerant.

flags.t: Nozzles: grey at 3.4 bar is about 284 L/ha
flags.d: Grey is ISO size 06: about 2.5 L/min at 3.4 bar. At 7.1 km/h that's about 284 L/ha on 75 cm nozzle spacing. The bucket test confirms it.
